strengths: Novel and well-motivated multimodal task combining forgery localization with natural language explanations, addressing a genuine gap in existing forensic detection methods
Large-scale, high-quality dataset (152,217 samples) with process-derived ground-truth masks ensuring pixel-perfect alignment and human-authored descriptions with rigorous quality control
Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive baselines (both specialist and general-purpose LVLMs), cross-dataset generalization (DQ_F++, SynthScars), and informative ablation studies
Solid baseline architecture with thoughtful design choices (FPN architecture, two-stage training pipeline) and strong empirical results (59.3 CIDEr, 73.67 IoU)
Clear presentation with excellent visualizations and strong reproducibility commitment (code, dataset, and pre-trained weights to be released)
weaknesses: Critical evaluation gap: absence of human evaluation for explanation quality, correctness, and spatial grounding; reference-based metrics (CIDEr, BLEU) designed for generic captioning may not capture explanation fidelity for forensic purposes; dramatic performance drop on SynthScars (2.2 vs. 59.3 CIDEr) raises concerns about metric reliability

Dataset construction lacks inter-annotator agreement (IAA) analysis across 30 annotators; no validation of ground-truth mask alignment with human perception; missing demographic diversity analysis (gender, age, ethnicity) and potential bias evaluation across demographic groups

Limited technical novelty: architecture primarily combines existing components (InstructBLIP, SAM, T5); FPN design is relatively standard; four pretraining losses used but only binary ablation provided; individual loss contributions not analyzed

Incomplete task formulation: omits binary real/fake classification under claim of 'saturation' supported by only two 2025 papers; heavy prompt engineering constrains outputs; no analysis of explanation faithfulness vs. post-hoc rationalization; unclear practical applicability

Insufficient FPN analysis: large gap between w/o FPN (51.7 CIDEr) and w/ FPN-GT (95.1 CIDEr) indicates region prompts are critical but unattainable; limited ablation results; no failure case analysis or investigation of struggle regions

Alignment between modalities not explicitly enforced: no mechanism ensuring text explanations correspond to predicted mask regions; cross-attention between Q-former and FPN doesn't guarantee spatial consistency

Limited qualitative analysis: only 4 example pairs shown; no systematic error categorization; missing analysis of performance by manipulation type during inference; no study of explanation diversity or correspondence to human descriptions

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifying that binary forgery masks lack interpretability and proposing textual explanations is a valid research direction
Substantial dataset contribution: 128,303 image-text pairs with thoughtful annotation pipeline including inconsistency inspection, quality control, and iterative refinement
Diverse manipulation coverage: Three different manipulation methods (face swapping, transformer-based and diffusion-based inpainting) with comprehensive dataset statistics
Reasonable technical approach: Sensible two-stage training with coordinate convolution and integration of SAM/InstructBLIP
Commitment to reproducibility: Authors promise to release dataset, code, and pretrained checkpoints
weaknesses: Critical FPN bottleneck severely undermines core claims: FPN achieves only 41% PLM, and the CIDEr gap between FPN-GT (48.1) and actual FPN (21.5) shows 55% performance drop, directly limiting interpretation quality

No human evaluation of interpretation quality: Despite claiming interpretability, the paper relies only on automatic metrics (BLEU/METEOR/CIDEr) without validating whether explanations are actually helpful or correspond to predicted forgeries

Single-dataset evaluation with no generalization evidence: Exclusively evaluated on author-constructed MMTT dataset with no cross-dataset validation on existing benchmarks (FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, ForgeryNet)
Limited technical novelty: ForgeryTalker primarily combines existing components (InstructBLIP, SAM, coordinate convolution) with straightforward FPN architecture using standard losses

Annotation quality not rigorously validated: No inter-annotator agreement (IAA) metrics reported; quality control is minimal (false positive screening only); improvement in second annotation phase undocumented
Unfair baseline comparisons: Baseline models not designed for this multi-modal interpretable segmentation task; results are not directly comparable
Limited analysis of results: No failure case analysis, no qualitative examples of generated interpretations with images, missing error analysis and insights into interpretation quality
Scope limitations undermine claims: Synthetic manipulations only (no real deepfakes), only facial images (limited generalization), 512×512 resolution, built on curated datasets

Core interpretability claims unsupported: While claiming interpretable explanations, the weak FPN (41% recall) means most predictions are based on incorrect region guidance, potentially misleading rather than explaining
